clue.text: Joiners employed in the rag trade?

definitions.text: Joiners employed in the rag trade?

parts.words: Joiners employed in the rag trade?
parts.note: joiners are not carpenters but small fasteners that join two edges of a garment, and the rag trade is the clothing business

explanation.surface: A question about carpenters taking jobs in the fashion industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiners' suggests woodworkers; here it means paired metal fasteners sewn onto clothes, and 'rag trade' is informal British for the garment industry.
explanation.definitionFit: These small paired metal fasteners join two edges of a garment, so they are joiners used by dressmakers.

clue.text: Do too much stuffing?

parts.note: stuffing reads like filling a turkey or cushion, but it means stuffing oneself with food

explanation.surface: A question about over-filling a cushion or a roast bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffing oneself to excess is gorging on more food than one needs.

clue.text: Where hokum production takes skill

indicators.note: takes signals that the reworked hokum holds the next piece within it
production suggests something made over, so the letters of hokum are worked into a new order

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A remark that producing nonsense convincingly is a craft in itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' alone is the definition, a cheeky one for a place: Sudan's capital. 'production' looks like staging a show but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sudanese capital is a place, and 'Where' stands for a location in a cryptic sense.

clue.text: In time kiss sweetheart, wound up

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces sit inside the word for time

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks a period of time in dates
X is the conventional written kiss at the end of a letter
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A romantic moment, timed with a kiss, that leaves someone hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' gives E, the middle letter of 'sweet'. 'wound up' looks like hurt or tense, but means brought to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A project that is terminated has been closed down or ended for good.

clue.text: Old copper is told and taken off

parts.note: D stands for the old penny, a copper coin of pre-decimal British money
to tell money is to count it, as a bank teller does

explanation.surface: A retired policeman informed and then removed from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old copper' looks like a former policeman; it is the pre-1971 British penny, abbreviated d.
explanation.definitionFit: A price reduced by a deduction has had money subtracted from it.

clue.text: Artist must stand in, certainly for a long time

indicators.note: in places the turned artist inside the word for certainly

parts.note: yes is an emphatic certainly

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up makes a word read from bottom to top, so it turns round

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone insists an artist must deputise, and has done so for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue a word that stands reads upwards. 'for' is a link, and RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: We say we have not met in ages, meaning a lengthy span of time.

clue.text: After taking second gratuity stop someone's salary

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity given for service
to end something is to stop it

explanation.surface: An employer, having pocketed a tip, cuts off an employee's pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After taking' only joins the pieces in order; it reads as a sequence of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed regular payment, especially to a clergyman or trainee, is a form of pay.

clue.text: People booking coach trips are cheated

definitions.text: People booking coach trips are cheated

parts.words: People booking coach trips are cheated
parts.note: coach passengers are literally carried somewhere on an outing, which in the idiom means being swindled

explanation.surface: A complaint that coach tour customers get swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being deceived or swindled is the literal state of passengers carried on a jaunt.

clue.text: Then I sent peer round to see capital water feature

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale of sending a nobleman on a tour of the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SERPENTINE is the lake in London's Hyde Park, a capital landmark; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This ornamental lake in Hyde Park is a famous body of water in London, the British capital.

clue.text: Mean to declare, given time

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone intends to make a statement once given a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb (intend) but is the noun for a statistical midpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the arithmetic midpoint of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Foreign bridge one takes mum to see

parts.note: to span a gap is to bridge it, and a span is a bridge
I is the Roman numeral for one
mum, as in keep mum, means silence, and sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A foreign bridge player takes their mother along to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but means silent, giving SH. 'takes' and 'to see' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from Spain makes something foreign to a British solver, an example of the broader term.

clue.text: First mate books function

parts.note: Eve was Adam's partner, the first mate in Genesis
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A first officer on a ship has duty to do with books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' suggests a ship's officer; it is Eve, the first wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A function can be a social gathering or occasion, like a party or dinner.

clue.text: Company with plants making vessels

parts.note: asters are daisy-like garden flowers

explanation.surface: A business with a factory producing ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plants' suggests factories; it means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Small ships that trade along a shoreline are a type of boat.

clue.text: Figure description is of her old cat, a cross-bred

indicators.note: cross-bred implies mixed stock, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Telling about a woman's elderly mongrel cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross-bred' rearranges HER OLD CAT A; 'is of' is a link. The definition is an adjective describing a solid shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for an eight-faced solid describes a geometric shape.

clue.text: Feast not as nice? Cut out pasta!

indicators.note: not tells us to leave something out of the word Feast

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A diet tip: skip the feast that is not so nice, and drop the pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not as' removes AS from FEAST to leave FET; 'out' rearranges NICE CUT into TUCCINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat ribbon noodles are an Italian variety of pasta.

clue.text: Coloured washer pushed back running water

indicators.note: pushed back means the coloured washer, taken together, is turned to read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour, so coloured can mean red
a washer is a flat ring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A dyed washing machine part shoved back into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washer' looks like laundry or plumbing; it is a ring shape. The ODER is a river between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is flowing water, and this one forms part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Persistent objections raised and upheld, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word for objections is read upwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

indicators.note: say signals a sound-alike of the word for upheld

parts.note: upheld means supported, borne aloft

explanation.surface: Complaints are aired and then sustained by a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BUTS into STUB; 'say' gives BORN, which sounds like BORNE (supported).
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate person keeps going and refuses to give way, being persistent.

clue.text: Roll round in liquid tar

indicators.note: in shows the round letter is placed inside the jumbled tar
liquid suggests something fluid, so the letters of tar flow into a new order

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone rolling around in molten road tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' turns TAR into RTA, and O goes 'in' it. 'Roll' is a noun, a list of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a list of names, and a duty roster is such a list.

clue.text: Connected with part of golf course, pointlessly

indicators.note: pointlessly asks for a compass point to be removed; E for east is the one dropped

parts.note: the rough is the long grass beside the fairway

explanation.surface: A remark about being linked to a stretch of a golf course for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' takes E (east, a compass point) from THE ROUGH. 'Connected' is the telephone sense, as in 'you're through'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On a phone call, being put through means being linked to the other party.

clue.text: The foreign soldiers' food is deplorable

parts.note: la is the French for the
men are soldiers, ordinary ranks
table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A complaint about the grub served to foreign troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The foreign' gives LA, French 'the'; 'table' means the meals provided.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regrettable deserves to be mourned, so it is deplorable.

clue.text: Ask June to drop Jack around one, after dance

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly

indicators.note: around shows the trimmed name wraps the letter for one
to drop tells us to remove the Jack letter from June

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks June to drop Jack and come to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop Jack' takes J from JUNE leaving UNE, which goes 'around' I. 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean ballroom rhythm, made famous by 'Begin the Beguine', is a type of dance.

clue.text: Sent on another course?

parts.note: another course suggests a fresh training course or meal, but it is a different route for traffic

explanation.surface: A question about someone enrolled on a second training course.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic diverted along a different route has been redirected.

clue.text: Absolute weirdo goes top less

indicators.note: going topless in a down clue means losing the first letter

parts.note: nutter is British slang for an eccentric or crazy person

explanation.surface: A complete oddball strips to the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes top less' removes the first letter of NUTTER. 'Absolute' is an adjective, as in 'utter nonsense'.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete or total, as in total nonsense, is the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Intolerant person shot in scrap

indicators.note: in places the word for shot inside the word for scrap

parts.note: a bit is a scrap or small piece
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: A prejudiced man is shot during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a gunshot and 'scrap' like a fight; they mean an attempt and a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot holds prejudiced views and will not accept other opinions.

clue.text: Man left quietly after advice

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A man slips out silently once he has had a word of counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance can take the form of guidance or counsel given to someone.

clue.text: One suspects live wire, twisted but inserted

indicators.note: inserted shows the twisted letters go into the word for live wire

parts.note: a doer is an energetic, active person

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of but are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for an electrician fitting a twisted live cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns BUT into UBT, 'inserted' into DOER. 'live wire' looks electrical but means an energetic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic distrusts what he hears, that is, he suspects.

clue.text: College fellow recalled excellent comment by Nigerian leader

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, makes the whole run read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
a note is a brief comment

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A former classmate remembers a fine remark by a Nigerian president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns AI NOTE into ETONIA. A1 (first-rate) is taken as letters AI. Eton is the elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: An old boy or pupil of Eton, the famous English school, is a member of that college.

clue.text: Hold a printer responsible for a dramatist

indicators.note: responsible for suggests these letters cause or make up something new, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: Blaming a print shop for a playwright's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible for' rearranges HOLD A PRINTER; 'a' is a link. HAROLD PINTER was the Nobel-winning English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Pinter wrote plays such as The Birthday Party, making him a playwright.
